lines.text: Where does gold come from? Look up.
lines.phonemes: wˌɛɹ dˈʌz ɡˈoʊld kˈʌm fɹʌm? lˈʊk ˈʌp.

lines.text: Gold is heavier than iron. Atoms that heavy are built by soaking up neutrons. One way is the fast way: a place packed with neutrons.
lines.phonemes: ɡˈoʊld ɪz hˈɛviɚ ðɐn ˈaɪɚn. ˈæɾəmz ðæt hˈɛvi ɑːɹ bˈɪlt baɪ sˈoʊkɪŋ ˌʌp nˈuːtɹɑːnz. wˈʌn wˈeɪ ɪz ðə fˈæst wˈeɪ: ɐ plˈeɪs pˈækt wɪð nˈuːtɹɑːnz.

lines.text: One place that does that: two neutron stars crashing together. In twenty seventeen, astronomers saw one happen, as ripples in space and as light.
lines.phonemes: wˈʌn plˈeɪs ðæt dˈʌz ðˈæt: tˈuː nˈuːtɹɑːn stˈɑːɹz kɹˈæʃɪŋ təɡˈɛðɚ. ɪn twˈɛnti sˈɛvəntˌiːn, ɐstɹˈɑːnəmɚz sˈɔː wˈʌn hˈæpən, æz ɹˈɪpəlz ɪn spˈeɪs ænd æz lˈaɪt.

lines.text: A neutron star is about as wide as a city, yet heavier than the Sun. A crash throws out hot matter, and some becomes heavy atoms. Scientists still debate what else makes heavy atoms.
lines.phonemes: ɐ nˈuːtɹɑːn stˈɑːɹ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt æz wˈaɪd æz ɐ sˈɪɾi, jˈɛt hˈɛviɚ ðɐn ðə sˈʌn. ɐ kɹˈæʃ θɹˈoʊz ˈaʊt hˈɑːt mˈæɾɚ, ænd sˌʌm bɪkˌʌmz hˈɛvi ˈæɾəmz. sˈaɪəntɪsts stˈɪl dᵻbˈeɪt wʌt ˈɛls mˌeɪks hˈɛvi ˈæɾəmz.

lines.text: Zoom in on your ring. Some of its gold may have been made in a crash like that, somewhere in space. Think of it as a souvenir.
lines.phonemes: zˈuːm ɪn ˌɔn jʊɹ ɹˈɪŋ. sˌʌm ʌv ɪts ɡˈoʊld mˌeɪhɐv bˌɪn mˌeɪd ɪn ɐ kɹˈæʃ lˈaɪk ðˈæt, sˈʌmwɛɹ ɪn spˈeɪs. θˈɪŋk ʌv ɪɾ æz ɐ sˌuːvənˈɪɹ.

lines.text: So some gold may be leftovers of a star crash. Stardust isn't a poem. It's chemistry.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ sˌʌm ɡˈoʊld mˈeɪ biː lˈɛftoʊvɚz əvə stˈɑːɹ kɹˈæʃ. stˈɑːɹdʌst ˌɪzənt ɐ pˈoʊᵻm. ɪts kˈɛmɪstɹi.

lines.text: Light time: the crash's ripples in space came first. Its visible light was spotted several hours later.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt tˈaɪm: ðə kɹˈæʃᵻz ɹˈɪpəlz ɪn spˈeɪs kˈeɪm fˈɜːst. ɪts vˈɪzᵻbəl lˈaɪt wʌz spˈɑːɾᵻd sˈɛvɹəl ˈaʊɚz lˈeɪɾɚ.

lines.text: Next: what happens at the edge of a black hole?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌʌt hˈæpənz æt ðɪ ˈɛdʒ əvə blˈæk hˈoʊl?
